Key Research Thinking Patterns: Efficiency-Driven Methodology: Prioritize computational efficiency (O(k) projection-gen in D2RP; RFPI O(nq)) while retaining strong theoretical guarantees
Theoretical Guarantees: Provide concrete distortion, reconstruction, and convergence bounds to underpin practical methods
Fairness and Bias Mitigation: Develop active learning and debiasing techniques to improve fairness without sacrificing accuracy
Data Distribution Awareness: Address distribution shifts between training/self-labeled data and population/test data (e.g., DeFastText)
Prototype-Centric Learning: Leverage prototypes to balance modalities and classes in multimodal tasks (PFBL)
Cross-Modal Representation: Combine pretrained embeddings with sophisticated fusion mechanisms to enhance multimodal tasks
Empirical Validation Across Diverse Domains: Demonstrate methods on regression, fairness, noise-robustness, spectral estimation, and multimodal detection
Summary Description: Dr. Chao Lan is a versatile ML researcher at the University of Oklahoma whose work spans theory-driven, efficient machine learning methods and real-world applications. His contributions illuminate a consistent theme: achieving strong performance with principled guarantees under practical constraints. He co-develops data-efficient projection techniques (D2RP) with reconstruction assurances for regression tasks, advances fairness in learning through decoupled models (D-FA2L) and debiasing self-labeled social data via kernel means matching (DeFastText), and tackles kernel-method bottlenecks through random-feature-based spectral-norm estimation (RFPI). Expanding into multimodal AI, he co-authors PFBL, a prototype-based fully balanced framework for DI-MFND that harmonizes modality and class balance via prototype-centric losses and cross-modal fusion. Across papers, Lan integrates theoretical insight with empirical validation on diverse datasets (MNIST, COMPAS, Twitter, Weibo, Fakeddit, Wine, Crime), employing tools such as BERT, CLIP, cross-transformers, and standard ML stacks to address scalable, responsible, and impactful ML challenges.
